findings.detail: Rating 7/10. These exec cases now assert rejection of the unreasoned exec construct, masking whether the subsequent stderr merge is checked. No case annotates only an exec on one line, then leaves `some-command 2>&1` unannotated on the next. Removing the block-wide stdout-uncertainty check would leave these snapshots satisfied while silently accepting that later diagnostic discard. The allowed escaped-exec control annotates both operations on the same line, so it does not cover this contract.
findings.fix: Add a static sample with a reasoned `exec >/dev/null` followed on a separate line by an unreasoned stderr merge. Assert the capture diagnostic and status 1, with a positive control that explicitly reasons both operations.
findings.title: write-scrut-tests: Relevant error output: Exec tests omit merges after an allowed exec.

strengths: Static samples cover redirect spellings, descriptor inheritance, reason boundaries, coprocesses and exec variants without executing sample programs.
Parser tests cover crashes, termination, invalid output and stale diagnostics after input-open failures.
Existing integration tests cover diagnostic replay and status preservation, while recorded plants demonstrate regression sensitivity.
summary: Reviewed the scoped changes, accompanying tests, existing integrations and recorded evidence by inspection. One Important coverage gap remains where exec-context rejection masks the later stderr-merge contract; no repository code or checks were run.
